about: Limits, placeholders and privacy patterns for loomi-connect-feedback. scripts/tool_feedback_report.py reads this file, so change a rule here and nowhere else. Each key is explained under notes. Names are compared normalised: lower case, with _, - and spaces removed (accountId and account_id are both accountid). Redaction is best effort; a lint blocker makes the plan's one change blocked, and a warning is shown with the plan.

notes.max_field_chars: submit_llm_feedback's limit on feedback and on what_i_tried (from its schema). A longer field is a blocker: shorten it, don't let the tool cut it.
notes.max_short_field_chars: submit_llm_feedback's limit on client and model (from its schema). Longer is a blocker.
notes.summary_max_chars: The one-line summary may be at most this long, and must be one line. Longer is a blocker.
notes.gap_types: The values submit_llm_feedback's gap_type accepts (from its schema). Any other value is a blocker.
notes.completion_estimate_min: Lowest completion_estimate the tool accepts. The skill always sends one, because the tool's description asks for it.
notes.completion_estimate_max: Highest completion_estimate the tool accepts. The top value means the request was fully done, which a problem report rarely is, so it's a warning.
notes.environments: Allowed values of --environment. Required, with no default. Engagement has no staging environment, so staging on an Engagement report is a warning.
notes.products: Allowed values of the report's product field.
notes.min_seconds_between_reports: submit_llm_feedback's rate limit (from its description): at most one report in this many seconds. After a 429, wait at least this long, and the Retry-After time if longer.
notes.max_reports_per_hour: submit_llm_feedback's hourly limit (from its description). Another reason to send one chosen report, never a list.
notes.allowed_arg_keys: The only argument names (normalised) whose string values are kept in the reproduction, and only when the value matches plain_value_pattern: enum-like settings such as filter_preset or sort. Every other string becomes a placeholder named after its normalised key (<accountid>, <q>). Numbers, booleans and ISO dates are kept unless the name is sensitive or the number has min_numeric_id_digits or more digits.
notes.plain_value_pattern: A kept argument value must match this: a short token with no spaces, slashes or @.
notes.excerpt_text_keys: In a response excerpt that parses as JSON, strings under these names (error and message text) are kept after free-text redaction, because they usually show the problem. Every other string becomes a placeholder.
notes.sensitive_name_words: A name (argument, JSON key or name: value / name=value pair in text) whose normalised form contains one of these is sensitive: its value is replaced, numbers included.
notes.sensitive_name_suffixes: A normalised name ending with one of these is sensitive too (accountid, customerids, lastmodifiedby).
notes.sensitive_names_exact: Normalised names that are sensitive only as a whole word (q, term, search): they usually carry shopper text.
notes.context_id_words: In free text, a value right after one of these words that contains a digit or a hyphen, underscore or dot (account 6012345, project acme-prod) is replaced by <word>.
notes.person_context_words: In free text, two or more capitalised words right after one of these (User Jane Doe, by Jane Doe) are replaced by <name>.
notes.token_patterns: Regular expressions for well-known secret token formats (cloud keys, OAuth tokens, chat and code-host tokens). Replaced by <token>, and a blocker if any are left.
notes.host_tlds: A bare host name (no scheme or path) ending in one of these is replaced by <host>. Hosts with a scheme or a path are always replaced by <url>.
notes.min_hex_id_chars: A run of at least this many hexadecimal characters with both a letter and a digit, or any UUID, counts as an ID and is replaced by <id>.
notes.min_numeric_id_digits: A run of at least this many digits counts as an ID and is replaced by <id>, in text and in arguments. A blocker if any are left.
notes.min_phone_digits: Digits written with separators (spaces, dots, brackets, hyphens) or a leading + that add up to at least this many count as a phone number (<phone>). Dates are left alone.
notes.min_opaque_token_chars: Lint only: a run of at least this many letters, digits, _ or - with both letters and digits is an unrecognised token or ID, and a blocker.
notes.allowed_url_prefixes: URLs that may stay in the report (this repository's docs). Any other URL is replaced by <url> and is a blocker if any are left, because a host or a query string can identify the customer.
notes.repo_doc_url: Public URL of docs/known-tool-behaviour.md. The report links to #L<line> of it when the problem comes from that file.
notes.known_marker: The text that marks an item in docs/known-tool-behaviour.md as worth reporting. list-known lists the lines that carry it, and build refuses a known_line without it.
notes.known_excerpt_chars: How much of the known-behaviour line (and its parent bullet) is quoted in the report.
notes.report_prefix: Start of the feedback text, so the Loomi Connect team can tell reports sent with this skill from others.
